published_honest_out_of_domain_documenta.name: honest_out_of_domain_documentation
published_honest_out_of_domain_documenta.note: 3/5 candidates have 0/5 AD gates passed — HONESTLY documented as OUT-OF-DOMAIN. This is red-team-defensible portfolio behavior: refuses to grant high-confidence scores to candidates outside training distributions. Candidates gated out: IPDA, TETA, DETA.

method: Rebuilt each of the 5 predictors' REAL training corpora as property-specific non-null-value subsets of the two SHA-pinned source datasets the KPI itself cites (openpoly_csv_sha256=8de5baf76f79610fe9173e63c65b824714aeb8445f9d670e1767956ea9db5eb3, radonpy_csv_sha256=4ee41d526db3d03eb5b83010672b4e63a4d51a114871a2187ca7fd57d30556a4), read from feedback/v2/normalized/{openpoly_properties,radonpy_pi1070}.jsonl.gz (the portfolio's own canonicalized copies of those exact files): Tg and water-contact-angle corpora = openpoly rows with a non-null value for that property (373 and 105 unique PSMILES respectively, matching each predictor's actual dataset_fixture_path-cited training receipt); density corpus = radonpy rows with non-null density (1077 unique SMILES); dielectric and refractive-index corpora = openpoly UNION radonpy non-null-per-property subsets, matching the 'mixed openpoly+RadonPy' methodology both predictors' own receipts declare (Push #34, #35). Computed standard ECFP4 fingerprints (RDKit GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect, radius=2, nBits=2048 -- the RDKit default, matching the KPI's own cited Rogers & Hahn 2010 ECFP/Morgan theory reference) for every corpus member and for each of the 5 candidate hardener SMILES exactly as published in the KPI's own candidate_cards[].smiles field, then computed Tanimoto nearest-neighbor similarity per candidate per predictor-corpus and compared against the published applicability_domain values. Swept 12 alternative radius/nBits configurations (radius in {1,2,3}, nBits in {512,1024,2048,4096}) plus an unfolded/sparse (collision-free) ECFP variant before settling on this configuration -- it uniquely reproduces DDS, TETA, and DETA's applicability-domain values EXACTLY (15/15 individual metrics, byte-identical to the published floats) across all three candidates, independently validating that this is genuinely the underlying methodology and not a coincidental fit.
objective: Independently reproduce the KPI's per-predictor applicability-domain Tanimoto-NN gate values from the exact corpora and fingerprint methodology it cites, and test whether the reproduced values change any candidate's gate PASS/FAIL outcome at the KPI's own published >=0.30 threshold -- which would falsify the honest_out_of_domain_documentation claim and the m-XDA composite-score ranking that depends on it.
pre_registered_refute_criterion: Attack fires (REFUTED) iff independent re-derivation of the per-predictor Tanimoto-NN applicability-domain gate values, using the KPI's own cited corpora (openpoly_csv_sha256/radonpy_csv_sha256) and cited fingerprint reference (Rogers & Hahn 2010 ECFP, RDKit default Morgan radius=2/nBits=2048), changes the gate PASS/FAIL outcome (at the KPI's own published >=0.30 threshold) for at least one candidate, thereby changing n_candidates_with_zero_ad_gates_passed or the named honest_out_of_domain_documentation candidate list.
primary_sources: Rogers, D. & Hahn, M. (2010), 'Extended-Connectivity Fingerprints', J. Chem. Inf. Model. 50(5):742-754 -- the ECFP/Morgan fingerprint methodology the attacked KPI itself cites in its theory list for applicability-domain computation.
OECD (2007) QSAR Validation Principle 3 (applicability domain) -- also cited by the attacked KPI.
recommended_followups: File a repair item (R-<id>) to recompute the decision-card KPI's applicability-domain gates with a documented, versioned fingerprint specification (radius, nBits, corpus-construction rule) and re-issue a v2 KPI with m-XDA correctly gated at 0/5, plus a superseding entry in RETRACTION-INDEX.md.
Commit the (currently entirely absent) generating script for this KPI to the repo so the decision card is independently reproducible end-to-end, not just its AD-gating layer.
Resolve the residual IPDA value-level reproducibility gap to rule out a second, currently-invisible defect that happens not to flip a gate outcome.

reproducibility.determinism_basis: no RNG, no wall-clock; corpus construction is a pure deterministic pass over the SHA-pinned gzipped normalized JSONL files with sorted() SMILES sets; two independent process invocations produced byte-identical stdout (sha256 a0ede137bea9ba013264332e550072062543b5b51af5fe807f0ff1dd4e599a8d both).

reviewer_reference.note: Reviewer key referenced for provenance only; no independent human review performed.

rights_check: No new external data source opened or acquired this fire. Both corpora (openpoly_properties, radonpy_pi1070) were already rights-cleared and normalized into feedback/v2/normalized/ by prior fires across the portfolio; this fire only read the existing normalized JSONL and computed structural fingerprints via the already-licensed RDKit toolkit.
scope_note: Does not question the DDS top-ranked finding or its 5/5 gate-pass status, which reproduces exactly. Does not fully resolve IPDA's residual value-level discrepancies (IPDA's raw AD values do not reproduce exactly under this methodology either, but its gate PASS/FAIL outcome is unaffected -- published and recomputed both give 0/5 gates passed for IPDA, so no ranking or out-of-domain-documentation claim depends on the exact IPDA numbers). Does not re-derive the underlying ML predictions (Tg_C_ml_prediction, density, dielectric, RI, contact-angle values themselves) -- only the applicability-domain gating layer. Does not assert the m-XDA discrepancy is deliberate fabrication versus an implementation bug (e.g. an off-by-one in a >= vs > boundary check, or a stale cached value); root cause is unestablished, only the observable inconsistency with the KPI's own stated, cited methodology.
why: 17/25 (68%) of the published per-candidate per-predictor AD Tanimoto-NN values reproduce EXACTLY under a methodology independently chosen to match the KPI's own cited corpora and cited fingerprint reference -- including a clean 15/15 sweep (100%) for DDS, TETA, and DETA across all 5 predictors each, which rules out corpus-selection or fingerprint-parameter mismatch as the general explanation and validates the reattack methodology as the real underlying computation. Against that validated methodology, m-XDA's density, dielectric, and refractive-index AD gates recompute to 0.28125 (a clean 9/32, structurally consistent with every other genuinely-computed Tanimoto ratio in this dataset), not the published 0.30 -- a suspiciously round value that is the ONLY one of 25 published AD numbers that is not an ugly small-integer fraction of a real bitset intersection/union. 0.28125 falls BELOW the KPI's own published >=0.30 admissibility threshold on all three gates. That flips m-XDA from 3/5 AD gates passed to 0/5: n_candidates_with_zero_ad_gates_passed should read 4 (adding m-XDA to IPDA/TETA/DETA), not the published 3, and the honest_out_of_domain_documentation metric's named candidate list is incomplete. Under the KPI's own composite-scoring formula (composite = ... x ad_reliability_multiplier, where ad_reliability_multiplier is the MEAN of the 5 per-predictor AD values), an honestly-gated m-XDA should have zero density/dielectric/refractive_index contribution to its domain-reliability score rather than the 0.30 credit it currently receives -- meaning m-XDA's published #2-ranked composite_score of 0.0377 was computed on an inflated domain-reliability input. The top-ranked candidate (DDS, the KPI's headline finding) is UNAFFECTED: its 5/5 gate-pass outcome and composite_score reproduce exactly under the same independently-validated methodology.
